item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01720","case1_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 120/2 as 60/2 = 30, then gives an unsupported final answer of 15.","case2_error":"Gives 2500 after correct unevaluated formulas that imply 4500.","reason":"Case 1 explicitly introduces an extra division during evaluation; case 2 supplies an unsupported number without showing a faulty calculation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01721","case1_error":"Reports 200 pairs instead of converting to the requested 400 individual plugs.","case2_error":"Reports the brother’s 11 cars instead of the three people’s combined 17 cars.","reason":"Both report a correctly calculated intermediate quantity as the requested answer, omitting the final conversion or aggregation.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J01722","case1_error":"Adds the 21, 4, and 18 books to the stated collection instead of including them among donated books.","case2_error":"Gives an unsupported 150 after correct formulas that imply 180 checkout shoppers.","reason":"Case 1 constructs an incorrect relationship between quantities; case 2 states correct relationships but supplies an unsupported final number.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01723","case1_error":"Treats one company’s 10 ads as all companies’ ads, omitting the factor of three.","case2_error":"Treats the $1000 commission as a base price and multiplies by 1.20 instead of dividing by 0.20.","reason":"Case 1 omits aggregation across companies; case 2 uses an incorrect relationship to recover a full price from its percentage.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01724","case1_error":"Uses four bags as the number of peanuts, ignoring the 30 peanuts per bag.","case2_error":"Incorrectly converts half a ton to 500 pounds and gives 15, unsupported even by its own formulas.","reason":"Case 1 confuses container count with item count. Case 2 uses a faulty unit conversion and an unsupported final number.","judgment":"different"}]}
